paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates how cosine similarity varies with the subset size \(|S|\) for two methods, “Weight averaging” and “QLoRA.” The x-axis is labeled \(|S|\) on a linear scale, spanning from 2 to 10 with major tick labels at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The y-axis is labeled “Cosine similarity” on a linear scale, ranging approximately from 0.1 to 0.35 with labeled ticks at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. The “Weight averaging” series is shown as a blue dashed line with filled square markers; it decreases from about 0.33 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.28 at 3, about 0.25–0.26 at 4–5, and then gradually declines to roughly 0.23 by \(|S|=10\), with small stepwise changes from \(|S|=6\) through 10 (around 0.24 down to ~0.23). The “QLoRA” series is shown as a green dashed line with filled circular markers; it decreases from about 0.29 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.26 at 3, drops to around 0.21 at 4, and continues decreasing more gradually to about 0.20 at 5, about 0.18 at 6, and approximately 0.17 to 0.166 by \(|S|=8\) through 10.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates cosine similarity values as a function of subset size \(|S|\) for two methods (“Weight averaging” and “QLoRA”). The x-axis is labeled \(|S|\), uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from 2 to 10, with major tick labels shown at 2-unit intervals (2, 4, 6, 8, 10). The y-axis is labeled “Cosine similarity.”, uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0.1 up to about 0.35, with major tick labels at 0.1 increments (0.1, 0.2, 0.3). The “Weight averaging” series is drawn as a blue dashed line with filled square markers, decreasing from about 0.33 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.23 at \(|S|=10\), with intermediate points around 0.28 (\(|S|=3\)), 0.25 (\(|S|=4\)), ~0.245 (\(|S|=5\)), and then gradually flattening near ~0.24–0.23 from \(|S|=6\) through 10. The “QLoRA” series is drawn as a green dashed line with filled circular markers, decreasing from about 0.29 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.165 at \(|S|=10\), passing through roughly 0.26 (\(|S|=3\)), ~0.21 (\(|S|=4\)), ~0.20 (\(|S|=5\)), ~0.185 (\(|S|=6\)), and then continuing downward more gradually around ~0.175 (\(|S|=7\)) to ~0.17 (\(|S|=8\)) and slightly below ~0.17 by \(|S|=9\)–10.
